reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to fund and register for Forsage BUSD slots using a referral link, rather than merely discussing the service. The associated Forsage screens present tiered entry options, participant earnings claims and an invite-ID automatic registration flow, while the description promotes a successful team and urges group members to start working. Together, these observations show recruitment-dependent participation and earnings claims central to the video's call to action.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker explicitly leaves room for hesitation: "if for example you are still not sure, please ask earlier" and asks those who do not understand to seek clarification. The page also warns visitors about fake resources. Those cautions matter when assessing whether this is deceptive solicitation: the speaker calls this preparation and says a fuller video will come later. The evidence supports an explanation of how to approach registration, not a promise that joining will pay off.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited balance and gas-fee instructions describe what a user would need for the process; they do not themselves promise earnings. Likewise, describing where to paste a referral link establishes an onboarding step, not what anyone receives from recruiting. The site's registration screen does not turn the speaker's invitation to ask questions into a guarantee of returns.

The speaker gives both instructions, while the page provides an invite-ID registration flow. A warning about fake sites concerns which site to use; it does not caution against the participation being promoted.

opening.argument: Judge, this is chiefly a walkthrough of wallet navigation. The speaker says they will explain how to prepare for registration, then describes opening the wallet, using its browser and checking that the network is BSC. The sampled screens show that progression from wallet to browser to registration page. The speaker calls it "preparation first, understanding first" and says a fuller video will follow. Explaining the steps a viewer would encounter is distinct from showing that a viewer joined, earned money or recruited anyone.

citations.quote: this time we will explain how to prepare the process
After that, make sure the network runs by a BSC if it is not a BSC network, replace it to a BSC network
so we'll do preparation first, understanding first for launched it later at night

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats procedural detail as proof of a completed recruitment scheme. But the cited speech says viewers should prepare a balance and paste a link; it does not report a completed transfer or a payout. The description's "successful big team" is promotional language, but it supplies no terms explaining how that team earns. The evidence can support a tutorial reading without assuming an outcome the video does not show.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the sequence a tutorial does not change what it teaches viewers to do. It specifies funds for slots, directs them to a shared referral link and advances them toward registration. The description also urges group members to work on the BUSD move. No completed payout is needed to recognize the video's active promotion of entry into that referral-based structure.

opening.argument: Judge, the observed referral link could be an ordinary promotional route into a paid service. The speaker identifies an amount for six slots and separately mentions gas fees, but does not say that buying slots guarantees a return or that the link pays its sharer. The registration screen asks the user to check an inviter ID; it does not display a commission owed to that inviter. A referral and a price alone do not establish that this video's central offer is recruitment income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution links slots, an inviter ID and a team description, but those items do not specify a commission schedule or show a participant being paid for a recruit. Even the cited page with tier information cannot establish from this video that a new viewer must recruit others to recover the stated slot cost. That missing mechanism matters before treating the referral itself as proof of deceptive recruitment.

citations.quote: Forsage ETH // Forsage TRX successful big team

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument asks for proof of an actual commission payment, but the concern is what viewers are urged to join. The speaker tells them to fund slots and use a shared referral link; the page presents inviter-based registration, and the description calls on a team to work on BUSD. Those elements make recruitment part of the promoted path even without a recorded payout.
